outputs.exact_statement: At $p=1009$ there is a finite $p$-local spectrum $X$ and an isomorphism $$BP_*X\ \cong\ BP_*/(p,v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4)$$ of graded $BP_*BP$-comodules, with the canonical quotient comodule on the right and its generator in degree zero.

For each $m\geq 1$, $I_m$ is an invariant ideal and $v_m$ is primitive modulo $I_m$. Modulo $I_m$, the coproducts of $t_i$, $i\leq m$, are the additive-composition coproducts. At the specialization that kills $p$ and all $v_i$, the resulting Hopf algebra is $$P=\mathbb F_p[t_1,t_2,\ldots],\qquad
 \Delta(t_i)=\sum_{\ell=0}^i t_\ell\otimes t_{i-\ell}^{p^\ell}.
 \label{fw:additive-hopf}$$

In the cobar cohomology with coefficients $R/I_4$, there is a scalar $e\in\mathbb F_p$ such that $$v_4\bigl(h_{1,4}+e v_4^{p-1}h_{1,0}\bigr)=0,
 \label{fw:v5-cohomology-relation}$$ where $h_{1,j}$ is represented by the primitive $t_1^{p^j}$.

If the coefficient comodule has no negative weights, then $$C^{s,w}\ne0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad w\geq s.
 \label{fw:positivity}$$

Suppose $s\geq1$, $w<u_{m+1}$, and $w-u_m<s-1$. Additive specialization identifies the normalized cobar complexes for $R/I_m$ and $P$, in weight $w$, in all three degrees $s-1,s,s+1$. It intertwines both adjacent differentials, and therefore induces an isomorphism on cohomology in degree $(s,w)$. The same conclusion in every cochain degree holds if $w<u_m$.

For every bounded-below $p$-local spectrum $Z$, the sphere-source Adams–Novikov spectral sequence has $$E_2^{s,t}(Z)=H^{s,t}\bigl(C^\bullet_\Gamma(BP_*Z)\bigr)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \pi_{t-s}Z.$$ It converges strongly, and the induced filtration in each stem is finite. The differential $d_r$ changes $(s,t)$ by $(r,r-1)$. The filtration-zero edge identifies $E_\infty^{0,*}$ with the image of the $BP$-Hurewicz map $\pi_*Z\longrightarrow BP_*Z$.

For bounded-below $p$-local spectra $Z_1,Z_2,Z_3$, an actual map $f:Z_1\wedge Z_2\to Z_3$ induces pairings of the Adams–Novikov spectral sequences, with the Leibniz rule on every page. The $E_2$ pairing is the cobar cup pairing induced by the exterior $BP$-homology pairing, and the $E_\infty$ pairing is the associated-graded pairing of the actual homotopy map $f$. No associativity of $f$ is needed. If $Z_1=Z_2=Z_3=Z$ has a binary two-sided unital multiplication and $BP_*Z=R/I$ is cyclic on its unit, the $E_2$ pairing is the ordinary multiplication on cobar cohomology with quotient-ring coefficients.

If $BP_*Z$ is concentrated in internal degrees divisible by $q$, then all pages of its Adams–Novikov spectral sequence have that same internal sparsity. Every possibly nonzero positive differential has length $r=qk+1$ for an integer $k\geq1$. In weight notation it changes $(s,w)$ to $(s+qk+1,w+k)$. In particular, a primitive coefficient of weight $u_n$ in filtration zero can have only targets $$(s,w)=(qk+1,u_n+k),\qquad k\geq1.
 \label{fw:primitive-targets}$$

Let $s=qk+1$, $w=u_4+k$, $k\geq1$. A nonzero normalized cobar group in degree $(s,w)$ with coefficients $R/I_4$ requires $$(q-1)k\leq u_4-1,\qquad
 w\leq\frac{qu_4-1}{q-1}<2u_4<p^4<u_5.
 \label{fw:preliminary-v4-bound}$$ For every such $k$, additive specialization is an isomorphism on cohomology in degree $(s,w)$, by an identification of the cochain groups of lengths $s-1,s,s+1$. No $v_4$ coefficient or $t_4$ bar occurs in any of those three cochain groups.

For every integer $M\geq0$, the cobar cohomology of $P$ admits a multiplicative, degreewise finite spectral sequence whose initial cohomology page is $$\Lambda(h_{i,j}:i\geq1,j\geq0) \otimes\mathbb F_p[b_{i,j}:i\geq1,j\geq0]. \label{may:initial-page}$$ The bidegrees and auxiliary filtrations are $$\begin{array}{c|c|c} & (s,w)& F_M\\ \hline h_{i,j}&(1,p^ju_i)&2i-1+M[j=0]\\ b_{i,j}&(2,p^{j+1}u_i)&p(2i-1+M[j=0]). \end{array}$$ Here $[j=0]$ is $1$ or $0$ according as $j=0$ or $j\neq0$. All differentials lower $F_M$. If an exterior generator is written $h_{[a,b)}=h_{b-a,a}$, its first differential is $$d_1 h_{[a,b)}=\sum_{a[may:initial-page].

The following cobar cohomology groups vanish.*

1.  *For $1\leq n\leq3$ and $k\geq1$, the group with coefficients $R/I_n$ in bidegree $$(s,w)=(qk+1,u_n+k).$$*

2.  *For $0\leq n\leq3$, choose $e_i\in\{0,1,2\}$ for $0\leq i\leq n$ and put $$U=\sum_{i=0}^n e_i u_i,\qquad
      \rho=\sum_{i=0}^n e_i\geq2.$$ For every $k\geq1$, the group with coefficients $R/I_{n+1}$ in bidegree $$(s,w)=(qk+1-\rho,U+k)$$ is zero.
A spectrum obtained from finitely many $p$-local sphere cells is the $p$-localization of a finite CW spectrum.

For $0\leq n\leq3$ there is a finite $p$-local cell spectrum $V(n)$ with a bottom-cell unit $\eta_n:S_{(p)}\to V(n)$ and a binary multiplication $$\mu_n:V(n)\wedge V(n)\longrightarrow V(n)$$ whose two unit identities hold. Its cells are indexed by subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n\}$, in dimensions $$\sum_{i\in S}(qu_i+1),
 \label{low:cell-dimensions}$$ and its $BP$-homology is the canonical quotient comodule $R/I_{n+1}$, generated in degree zero by the bottom unit. In particular, we may fix $$Y=V(3),\qquad BP_*Y=R/I_4,
 \label{low:Y}$$ with such a binary two-sided unital multiplication.
For the spectrum $Y$ of Proposition 13, $\pi_0Y=\mathbb F_p$ and $p\operatorname{id}_Y$ is nullhomotopic.

The groups in [may:obstruction-degrees] are identified with $H^{s,w}(P)$. Their May page has only positions $0,1,2,3$, and it is zero unless $k\leq p+2$. For $k\geq2$, only positions $0,1,2$ can occur.

In bidegree $(s,w)=(q+1,u_4+1)$ the complete initial May page consists of $$acb B^{p-2},\qquad acybz B^{p-3}. \label{may:first-target-list}$$ The first is not a splitting cycle and the second is a splitting cycle. In bidegree $(q+1,u_5+1)$ the complete list is given in Table 2. The four entries of exterior length three or five have no nonzero splitting cycle in their span.

Multiplication by the primitive class $h_{1,4}$ is injective on actual cobar cohomology in bidegree $(q+1,u_4+1)$: $$H^{q+1,u_4+1}(P)\xrightarrow{\ h_{1,4}\ }
 H^{q+2,u_5+1}(P).$$
In the Adams–Novikov spectral sequence for $Y$, one has $d_{q+1}(v_4)=0$.

For $k\geq2$ the complete initial May page in [may:obstruction-degrees] is Table 19; all other values of $k$ give an empty page. Put $N_0=(p-1)^2$ and $N=p(p-1)-2$.*
| *$k$* | *Initial May monomials* | |:-------:|:----------------------------------------------------------------------| | *$2$* | *$xac B A^{p-2}C^{p-2}$, $\quad xacyz A^{p-2}C^{p-2}$* | | *$p-1$* | *$y B^3 A^{N_0-3}$, $\quad b B^2 A^{N_0-2}$, $\quad ybz B A^{N_0-2}$* | | *$p$* | *$cyb A^{N+1}$, $\quad ayb B A^N$* | *Every initial May monomial for the later $v_4$ obstruction bidegrees.*

The following initial-page tests give surjections on actual cobar cohomology.* 1. *If every monomial of [may:initial-page] in bidegree $(s,w)$ uses only generators with $i\leq r$, then $H^{s,w}(P_r)\longrightarrow H^{s,w}(P)$ is surjective.* 2. *Put $A=b_{1,0}$. If every initial-page monomial in bidegree $(s,w)$ contains $A^a$, then multiplication by the actual cocycle representing $A^a$ gives a surjection $$H^{s-2a,w-pa}(P)\longrightarrow H^{s,w}(P).$$* *These conclusions also transport through additive comparisons that identify the source and target cohomology groups and commute with the indicated maps.

For $r=3$ there is an isomorphism of bigraded algebras $$\label{frob:kernel-cohomology}
 H^*(K_3;\mathbb F_p)
   =\Lambda(x,a,c)\otimes\mathbb F_p[A,B,E].$$ The exterior generators have cohomological degree one and weights $1,u_2,u_3$, and the polynomial generators have cohomological degree two and weights $p,pu_2,pu_3$, respectively. Write $\xi=t_1^p$, $\eta=t_2^p$ for quotient coordinates. With the right-conjugation convention, the quotient coaction is $$\begin{aligned}
 x&\BeginAccSupp{method=hex,unicode,ActualText=27FC}\OriginalLongmapsto\EndAccSupp{}x,&
 a&\BeginAccSupp{method=hex,unicode,ActualText=27FC}\OriginalLongmapsto\EndAccSupp{}a+x\xi,&
 c&\BeginAccSupp{method=hex,unicode,ActualText=27FC}\OriginalLongmapsto\EndAccSupp{}c+x\eta+a\xi^p,\label{frob:exterior-action}\\
 A&\BeginAccSupp{method=hex,unicode,ActualText=27FC}\OriginalLongmapsto\EndAccSupp{}A,&
 B&\BeginAccSupp{method=hex,unicode,ActualText=27FC}\OriginalLongmapsto\EndAccSupp{}B+A\xi^p,&
 E&\BeginAccSupp{method=hex,unicode,ActualText=27FC}\OriginalLongmapsto\EndAccSupp{}E+A\eta^p+B\xi^{p^2}.
 \label{frob:polynomial-action}
\end{aligned}$$ Products in these formulas mean coefficient times quotient coordinate. In particular, $xac$ and $A$ are invariant. Exterior degree and polynomial degree are separately preserved. The corresponding statements for $r=2$ omit $c$ and $E$.

For $Q_2$ or $Q_3$, at any positive rescaled weight $w | *Rescaled weight* | *Cohomological degree* | *May monomials* | |:------------------|:-----------------------|:----------------| | *$p(p-1)$* | *$2p-4$* | *—* | | *$p(p-1)$* | *$2p-3$* | *$zC^{p-2}$* | | *$p(p-2)$* | *$2p-4$* | *$C^{p-2}$* | | *$p(p-3)$* | *$2p-5$* | *—* | | *$p+2$* | *$1,3$* | *—* | | *$p+2$* | *$2$* | *$yb$* | | *$2p+2$* | *$2$* | *—* | | *$2p+2$* | *$3$* | *$ybz$* | | *$3p+2$* | *$3$* | *—* | | *$2$* | *$1,3$* | *—* | *The classes $C^{p-2}$ and $zC^{p-2}$ in the table are nonzero in actual quotient cohomology. There is also a nonzero class $\upsilon$ of degree two and weight $p+2$, detected by $yb$, and $\upsilon z$ is nonzero in degree three and weight $2p+2$.
At $s=4p-3$ and $w=u_4+2$, the cobar cohomology group in Table 19 is zero.
Put $N_0=(p-1)^2$. At $s=2N_0+1$ and $w=u_4+p-1$, the cobar cohomology group in Table 19 is zero.

The obstruction groups in bidegrees $$(s,w)=(2q+1,u_4+2),\qquad (s,w)=(q(p-1)+1,u_4+p-1)$$ vanish in the additive cobar calculation of Table 19. Among its rows with $k\geq2$, only the row $k=p$ remains to be addressed.

Every class of $E_2^{5,W}(Y)$ survives to homotopy. Moreover, $$\label{top:alpha-gamma-vanishing}
 \pi_{q(W+1)-6}Y=0.$$

There are sphere classes $$\alpha\in\pi_{q-1}S^0_{(p)},\qquad \beta\in\pi_{pq-2}S^0_{(p)}$$ detected respectively by $[t_1]$ and the divided coproduct $b_{1,0}$. The former generates a cyclic group of order $p$, and $$\pi_iS^0_{(p)}=0\qquad(0[top:An-surjection].

Let $U_0$ be a connective $p$-local spectrum with $$H_0(U_0;\mathbb Z_{(p)})=\mathbb Z_{(p)},\qquad
 H_{q-1}(U_0;\mathbb Z_{(p)})=\mathbb Z/p,$$ and with all other positive integral homology through degree $q$ zero. Let $b_0:S^0\to U_0$ induce an isomorphism on $H_0$, and suppose the reduced power $\mathcal P^1$ of the bottom mod-$p$ cohomology class is nonzero. Then there is a three-cell spectrum $$Q=\bigl(S^0\vee S^{q-1}\bigr)
       \cup_{(a\alpha,\,up)}e^q$$ and a map $Q\to U_0$ whose restriction to $S^0$ is $b_0$. Here $u\in\mathbb Z_{(p)}^\times$ and $a\in\mathbb F_p^\times$.
The image of $\alpha\beta^p$ in $\pi_*Y$ is zero.

For $T=\operatorname{Sym}^{p-1}(\Sigma^{-q}C(\alpha))$, the module $BP_*(DT\wedge Y)$ is free over $R/I_4$ with basis $1,r,\ldots,r^{p-1}$, where $r^k$ has weight $k$. Its coaction is $$\label{top:translated-comodule}
 r^k\BeginAccSupp{method=hex,unicode,ActualText=27FC}\OriginalLongmapsto\EndAccSupp{}\sum_{j=0}^k\binom kjr^jt_1^{k-j}.$$ The induced homology map of $D\varepsilon_T\wedge1_Y:Y\to DT\wedge Y$ is the inclusion of constants. The powers of $r$ denote basis elements; no multiplication on $DT$ is asserted.

For $d=|\beta|=pq-2$, the actual stable map $$\label{top:null-composite}
 f:\Sigma^dT\xrightarrow{\ \Sigma^d\varepsilon_T\ }S^d
       \xrightarrow{\ \beta\ }S^0
       \xrightarrow{\ \eta\ }Y$$ is nullhomotopic.

If $\gamma\in\pi_{qW-5}Y$ represents a class of $E_2^{5,W}(Y)$, then $$\label{top:beta-annihilation}
 \beta^K\gamma=0,\qquad K=p(p-2)+1.$$ Only the binary two-sided unit identities for $\mu$ are needed.
Every class in $E_2^{qp+1,u_4+p}(Y)$ is zero on the Adams–Novikov page $E_{qp+1}$.

coverage.checked_domain: Exhaustive integer triples in {-1,0,1}^3 at p in {3,5,7,1009}; finite evaluations only, not universal polynomial or homotopy certification.
coverage.oracle_basis: Candidate evaluates the integral binomial sum with exact fmpz arithmetic; oracle independently evaluates the right-hand power quotient using exact Python integers. Every output integer is rechecked; no solver witnesses are used.
